html:
The global order faces significant instability as President Trump announces plans to declare the Strait of Hormuz US territory "soon," a move Iran vehemently rejects, insisting the strategic waterway is an inseparable part of its territorial waters. This escalating rhetoric comes amidst ongoing conflict and reports of attacks on tankers in the Strait, severely reducing shipping traffic.

US-Iran Tensions: President Trump's declaration plans for the Strait of Hormuz, which he states will occur "soon" after Iran is defeated, are met with strong defiance from Tehran, with its Deputy Foreign Minister asserting the Strait cannot be seized by tweets or force. Simultaneously, Iran claims Qatar captured three Iranian fighter pilots at the start of the US-Iran war, a claim Qatar denies, stating it found remains of one pilot. Shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz remains at just 17 percent of pre-war levels, following reports of a bulk carrier hit by a projectile and condemnation from Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Jordan regarding Iranian attacks on ADNOC tankers. President Trump has stated that higher gas prices are a worthwhile cost to prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons.

Middle East Conflicts: Escalation in the Middle East saw Israeli strikes kill at least 11 people in southern Lebanon, with Israel's military stating targets were "Hezbollah terror infrastructure" in response to actions against its soldiers, which seriously injured three. Hezbollah has threatened appropriate retaliation, with Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem criticizing the Lebanese state and affirming resistance. Meanwhile, settler attacks in the West Bank persist despite international outcry, leading Jordan, Qatar, and the OIC to condemn the actions, and an Israeli human rights group to warn of accelerating 'ethnic cleansing.' Israel also carried out a strike in Gaza, killing one person.

Global Disasters: Rescuers continue to search for survivors in Indonesia after a powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake killed at least 47 people and destroyed hundreds of buildings. In Zimbabwe, the death toll from a ferry accident on Lake Kariba has risen to 68, with 22 more bodies recovered. Hawaii is bracing for a potential direct hit by Hurricane Lala, which could be the first in 34 years, while a severe Ebola outbreak in DR Congo continues to claim a life every 30 minutes, with over 2,100 deaths reported. The US is also experiencing a massive egg recall due to a salmonella outbreak affecting nearly 1.6 million dozen eggs.

Global Security & Policy: Australia's New South Wales will launch a gun buyback scheme after the Bondi Beach attack, with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese inviting all states to join and noting the country now has more guns than at the time of the Port Arthur massacre. In East Asia, South Korean President Lee Jae-myung has proposed talks with Pyongyang to formally end the Korean War, which has technically been ongoing for 70 years. Morocco has detained over 100 migrants attempting to cross into Spain’s Ceuta amidst heightened security, following recent social media calls for mass crossings. In Afghanistan, the Taliban faces pressure from insurgents five years after retaking power, with a devastating impact on the education of girls and boys, and thousands of Afghans who aided US troops now fear losing their green cards.

Domestic & European Affairs: President Trump's legal team is accusing the BBC of harassment in a Panorama lawsuit, while President Trump himself has asked the Supreme Court to allow White House ballroom construction to continue, citing security. Democratic lawmakers are calling for an investigation into conditions on the long-deployed USS Lincoln, whose crew's families say President Trump should be "ashamed" of his comments regarding their deployment. Jason Arday, a Cambridge professor, was found dead after recently resigning amidst a plagiarism row. Elsewhere, Belgium continues to battle one of its worst wildfires, scorching over 2,700 hectares, and France’s Constitutional Court has rejected a law that would have banned social media for children under 15, citing freedom of expression concerns. Construction workers in Belgium also unearthed $10 million in gold during renovations.
